region: Cutchogue · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: Pellegrini Vineyards sits on Main Road in Cutchogue, in the heart of Long Island’s North Fork. Bob and Joyce Pellegrini founded it in 1982 with the aim of making the very best wine the North Fork could offer, and the winery reflects Bob’s lifelong interest in food, wine and design, with a courtyard and tasting room set among roughly 30 acres of gently rolling vines, unusual terrain on the mostly flat North Fork. Bob died in 2015; Joyce and the team carry on his vision.

Winemaker Zander Hargrave grew up at Hargrave Vineyard, founded by his parents, Alex and Louisa Hargrave, pioneers of Long Island wine. The estate’s oldest Chardonnay vines date to 1982. Pellegrini makes two styles of Chardonnay: an Estate bottling fermented in large French oak puncheons, and this one, kept entirely out of oak in stainless steel so the fruit and the maritime freshness of the site come through unadorned.

Expect honeydew melon and chamomile leading to a citrus and mango finish, and a local reviewer of an earlier vintage found it smooth, with melon and tropical flavors. It is a bright, easygoing counterpoint to Pellegrini’s richer Estate Chardonnay. The tasting room, open year-round, pours it alongside the Estate Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Encore, the Bordeaux blend made only in the best vintages.
facts: Fermented and aged in stainless steel, no oak
North Fork of Long Island; estate planted from 1982
